title: DSL Rules
subject: gated-scoped-ac

claims.text: Any access-control business intention is expressible.
Rules adapt to any business model and any storage schema.
Roles are the unit of access; hierarchies compose them.
Rules can traverse entity relationships through joins declared in the schema.
Rules are declarations — meaning is independent of order or evaluation strategy.

**Why.** A declarative language is auditable and changeable without touching code. Every product needs the same shapes — roles, inheritance, conditional grants over related entities — and a shared DSL captures them once.

**How.** Roles bundle access. Each rule attached to a role pairs a context (preconditions on the bag) with a target (the slice of an entity granted, possibly traversing relationships through joins). Hierarchies declare inheritance: a role automatically grants everything its descendants grant.

**Why this way.** Declarations decouple meaning from evaluation. The same rules behave identically regardless of when, where, or in what order they are consulted, which is what makes them auditable. Roles + hierarchies + relationship traversal cover the access-control intentions products actually need without leaking product knowledge into the language.

reference.statement: **What.** The language consumers use to declare access control: roles, hierarchies among roles, and per-operation rules that pair context preconditions with target scopes.

The examples in this document use a fictional document-management product: workspaces contain folders, folders contain documents, users belong to workspaces through memberships, optionally grouped into teams. None of this vocabulary is built into the library — it is what the consumer declares in their schema and rules.

claims.text: The library reads four fields:

reference.statement: A role is a named bundle of access rules over one entity, for one or more operations. The library treats the role name as an opaque identifier; the role's meaning is whatever its rules grant.

snippets.caption: ts

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Field | Required | Meaning |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `entity` | yes | Which entity the rules act on. Must be declared in the schema. |
| `actions` | yes | Which operations this role contributes to. A role with `["read"]` does not affect a `delete` decision. |
| `accessRules` | yes | List of rules. Order has no semantic effect; rules combine by union. |
| `fields` | no | Column allowlist. `undefined` = all columns. |

claims.text: The library reads only its four fields and ignores the rest. Extending is the canonical way to keep one declaration object per role without contaminating the engine.

reference.statement: The library type is intentionally minimal. Consumers needing product-specific fields (UI labels, signals for external systems, anything outside engine evaluation) extend the type:

snippets.caption: ts

claims.text: **context** — a list of scopes that must all match against the bag for the rule to apply. Empty `context` always applies.
**target** — a list of scopes that together describe the rows reachable by this rule. Empty `target` grants the entity unrestricted (all rows).
Multiple rules on a role combine by union: any rule that matches contributes its target.

snippets.caption: ts

claims.text: The parser rejects unquoted literals and unprefixed dotted RHS values at boot.

reference.statement: Both context and target scopes use the same `LHS:RHS` shape. The class of each side is decided by its sigil:

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Class | Sigil | Example | Where it appears |
|-------|-------|---------|------------------|
| Entity path | bare | `document.workspaceId` | LHS only — a path into an entity declared in the schema |
| Subject path | `$` | `$session.user.id` | RHS only — a path into the runtime bag |
| Literal | `'…'` | `'team'` | RHS only — a quoted string constant |

snippets.code:
Rule         = ContextScope | TargetScope
ContextScope = EntityPath ':' Literal              (no subject paths on context RHS)
TargetScope  = EntityPath ':' (SubjectPath | Literal)
EntityPath   = Identifier ('.' Identifier)+
SubjectPath  = '$' Identifier ('.' Identifier)+
Literal      = "'" non-apostrophe-chars "'"
Operator     = ':' | ':!'                          ('!' = not equal)

reference.topic: Reference › Why context RHS is literal-only
reference.statement: Context scopes are preconditions evaluated before any target work happens. Allowing subject paths on context RHS produces resolution-time circular dependencies (the subject the context tests may itself depend on the result of the rule). Restricting context RHS to literals removes the cycle and keeps preconditions pure.

snippets.code:
workspace.type:'personal'        → workspace's type is "personal"
workspace.type:!'archived'       → workspace's type is anything except "archived"
document.ownerId:$session.user.id    → document's owner is the caller

claims.text: Each key is a role name. Its value is a (possibly empty) object of descendants. `{}` = leaf role (no further inheritance). The structure is purely declarative — order is irrelevant, depth is unbounded, the same role may appear under multiple parents.

A user assigned `workspace_owner` effectively holds `workspace_owner` + `manage_workspace_members` + `manage_workspace_documents` + `view_workspace_documents`. The library expands assigned roles through the hierarchy at evaluation time — see SCOPE-FILTER (`SCOPE-FILTER.md`).

reference.statement: Roles compose through declared inheritance, expressed as a generic nested tree. A parent role automatically grants everything its descendants grant, plus its own rules.

snippets.caption: ts

reference.topic: Reference › No special keys, no auto-injection

claims.text: The library also **never auto-adds roles** to a request. If a product wants every authenticated user to inherit a baseline set (e.g. "manage own profile"), the consumer is responsible for including those role names in the `assignedRoles` array passed to `expandRoles`.

Organizing the hierarchy by archetype, baseline-vs-org, or any other product taxonomy is a consumer concern — express it in how the consumer composes the tree from partials, not by relying on library-special keys.

reference.statement: The hierarchy is a flat top-level map of roots. The library does not interpret any key as special (no `account_baseline`, no `orgTypes`, no archetype concept). Every root is a sibling.

snippets.caption: ts

claims.text: The schema records *what exists*, not *what AC does with it*. Adding a role never requires schema changes.

reference.statement: The DSL stays storage-agnostic by referencing entities through a schema map the consumer declares. The schema is the storage-binding for the engine — it tells the resolver which table backs each entity name, what its id column is, and which columns are reachable.

snippets.caption: ts

claims.text: Reads as: "members whose `organizationId` joins to an `organization` whose `type` equals `'platform_admin'`."
The resolver compiles this into a traversal filter:
The engine assumes the FK joins to the toEntity's `id` column. (This is the convention; explicit FK metadata is not declared in the schema.)
Multi-hop chains compose by adding arrows:
Each hop is one LEFT JOIN at SQL emit time. Hops sharing the same `(fromEntity → toEntity)` across multiple roles deduplicate to a single JOIN.
The role's `entity` is always the *target* — the thing the filter narrows. The chain starts on the target entity's column and walks outward.

reference.statement: A target scope can chain across foreign keys with `→`. Each arrow says "follow this column to the joined entity's id":

snippets.caption: ts

reference.topic: Reference › Direct vs. traversal at a glance

snippets.code:
direct (no arrow)         org.id:$session.org.id
                          └── condition on the role's entity itself

traversal (one arrow)     member.organizationId → organization.type:'platform_admin'
                          └── follow FK, then condition on the joined entity

traversal (multi-hop)     document.folderId → folder.workspaceId → workspace.ownerId:$session.user.id
                          └── follow chain of FKs, condition on the last

claims.text: When multiple roles contribute to the same decision, fields combine permissively:
`undefined` ∪ anything = `undefined` (the broadest wins)

reference.statement: The `fields` property on a role definition restricts which columns the resolver permits the caller to read.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| `fields` value | Meaning |
|----------------|---------|
| `undefined` | All columns reachable |
| `["id", "title"]` | Only these columns reachable |

claims.text: Every entity path resolves to an entity declared in the schema.
Every subject reference (`$foo.bar`) names a subject declared in the consumer's `subjects` list.
Every literal is properly quoted and closed.
Every hierarchy edge points to a declared role; no cycles.
A failure throws with the offending role and rule pinpointed. Misconfigurations die at boot, not at runtime.
